model: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M (llama.cpp b11380), RTX 3050 Ti 4 GB, all layers on GPU
prompt: CSV rows -> JSON array (structured extraction; output copies tokens from the prompt), 300 max tokens, greedy
reading: flash attention: ~8% faster than off (54.5 vs 50.3 tok/s); output text differs slightly from the other kernel path

KV cache q8_0: allocation halves (144 -> 76.5 MB at 4096 ctx; 36.0 -> 19.1 KiB/token) at ~3.5% lower speed here; output text changed vs f16 (greedy decoding is sensitive to the small numerical change). Worth it when the KV cache is the memory problem (long context, many slots), not for a 3B model with 144 MB of cache

n-gram speculation: lossless (identical text to baseline) and 129 tok/s on the repeated requests, BUT the first measured request ran at 55.0 tok/s, equal to the baseline: the speedup appears once the same or similar output has already been seen in the session. Expect gains for repeated/templated outputs (RAG, extraction, SQL patterns), not for a first-time generation
caveats: one model (3B Q4_K_M), one prompt, 3 timed runs per setting, greedy decoding; speeds include prompt processing
n-gram numbers are inflated by repetition of an identical request (see reading)
a draft-model speculation run was not measured (no small same-family GGUF was prepared)
text differences are with respect to the f16-KV, flash-attn-auto baseline; they were not scored for correctness
